### Summary of Formalization

- **Functional Implementation** ([23_is_prime.lean](file:///home/user/lean_project/Veribench/23_is_prime.lean#L23-L47)):
  - `checkDivisors` recursively tests candidate divisors of the form $6k - 1$ (`i`) and $6k + 1$ (`i + 2`) starting at `5` up to $\lfloor\sqrt{n}\rfloor$.
  - `is_prime` handles $n \le 1$, $n \in \{2, 3\}$, multiples of $2$ or $3$, and delegates to `checkDivisors` for $n \ge 4$.
- **Unit Tests** ([23_is_prime.lean](file:///home/user/lean_project/Veribench/23_is_prime.lean#L51-L74)):
  - Verified docstring examples, test suite cases, and additional edge/prime/composite cases using `native_decide` and `#eval`.
- **Pre-condition, Properties, and Post-condition** ([23_is_prime.lean](file:///home/user/lean_project/Veribench/23_is_prime.lean#L82-L303)):
  - `Pre`: $0 \le n$.
  - `le_one_not_prime_prop` & `le_one_not_prime_thm`: $n \le 1 \to \text{is\_prime } n = \text{false}$.
  - `small_primes_prop` & `small_primes_thm`: $(n = 2 \lor n = 3) \to \text{is\_prime } n = \text{true}$.
  - `div_two_or_three_not_prime_prop` & `div_two_or_three_not_prime_thm`: $n > 3 \to (n \bmod 2 = 0 \lor n \bmod 3 = 0) \to \text{is\_prime } n = \text{false}$.
  - `prime_divisibility_prop` & `prime_divisibility_thm`: $\text{is\_prime } n = \text{true} \leftrightarrow (1 < n \land \forall d : \mathbb{Z},\, 1 < d \to d < n \to \neg(d \mid n))$.
  - `nat_prime_iff_prop` & `nat_prime_iff_thm`: $\text{is\_prime } n = \text{true} \leftrightarrow (0 \le n \land \text{Nat.Prime } n.\text{toNat})$.
  - `Post_prop`: Conjunction of all five properties.
- **Property-Based Tests (PBTs)** ([23_is_prime.lean](file:///home/user/lean_project/Veribench/23_is_prime.lean#L308-L357)):
  - Randomized PBTs via `#eval Plausible.Testable.check` and exhaustive bounded PBTs over $[0, 200)$ for every property and `Post_prop`.
- **Correctness Theorem** ([23_is_prime.lean](file:///home/user/lean_project/Veribench/23_is_prime.lean#L364-L370)):
  - `is_prime_correct`: proves `Pre n → Post_prop n`.
- **Imperative Implementation, Tests, and Equivalence Theorem** ([23_is_prime.lean](file:///home/user/lean_project/Veribench/23_is_prime.lean#L378-L478)):
  - `is_prime_imp` implemented with `Id.run do` and mutable loop variables `i` and `isPrime`.
